speaker: A. V. Zelevinsky
title: Verma-module multiplicities and Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomials
summary: The actual section begins on P000995 and continues onto P000996, before Beilinson speaks. It recalls highest-weight modules and finite-length Verma modules, reduces composition multiplicities to a regular integral Weyl orbit, and reports the proved Kazhdan--Lusztig multiplicity conjecture. A subsequent coefficient interpretation anticipates the separate Jantzen-filtration discussion. The catalog page span includes earlier Schwarz material; it is not a mathematical boundary.

speaker: A. A. Beilinson
title: Category O and restricted contragredient duality
summary: The named intervention occupies P000996, between the coefficient question and S. Gelfand. It introduces category \(\mathcal O\), restricted duality, and the dual Verma module as preparation for the Jantzen filtration. The notebook confuses the sign of the locally nilpotent nilradical and does not spell out the anti-involution required for a duality preserving highest-weight category \(\mathcal O\).

speaker: S. I. Gelfand
title: Contravariant forms, Jantzen layers and deformation directions
summary: The named section starts at the foot of P000996 and ends above the new Zelevinsky heading on P000997. It describes the contravariant form, identifies Verma modules through PBW vectors, deforms the weight by \(t\rho\), and introduces the order-of-vanishing filtration. It asks whether changing \(\rho\) preserves layer multiplicities and links coefficients to Schubert geometry. Moving lifts, normalization of polynomial degrees, and the distinction between ordinary and intersection cohomology require explicit repair.

speaker: A. V. Zelevinsky
title: Finite-dimensional weight multiplicities and affine Weyl polynomials
summary: The section begins near the foot of P000997. Gelfand inserts the type-A alternant character formula and a Cauchy-determinant exercise. Zelevinsky then identifies weight multiplicities with values of affine Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomials, followed by an incompletely specified extension to all Kac--Moody algebras. The latter is kept apart from the finite-dimensional Verma-module multiplicity theorem.

speaker: A. G. Elashvili
title: Primitive enveloping algebras and Frobenius semidirect products
summary: The actual intervention occupies the lower part of P000998. It asks Jacobson\textquotesingle s primitivity question, excludes nonzero semisimple and nilpotent examples, gives affine and binary-cubic semidirect products, and asserts a restricted classification with a further construction method. The exact 1982 announcement identifies the older Ooms criterion and supplies the missing reductive hypotheses; its full classification is broader than the notebook\textquotesingle s two examples.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Nonstandard analysis, relaxation oscillations and surreal sign sequences
summary: The section begins on P000999 and continues to the Krichever heading on P001000. It reports Cartier\textquotesingle s November 1981 Bourbaki exposition of Reeb\textquotesingle s methods, gives the van der Pol singular limit and its Rayleigh form, and sketches Cartier\textquotesingle s random-element quotient using a zero-one finitely additive measure. It then introduces surreal numbers through arrow sequences. The ultrapower and surreal field are distinct constructions; the open-interval probability codomain and finite-arrow halving rule require mathematical emendation.

speaker: I. M. Krichever
title: An elliptic matrix-function fragment
summary: Only the bottom of P001000 is headed Krichever. It names joint work with Brazovskii and Dzyaloshinskii, writes an unspecified ascending union, and displays a sigma-product matrix function on an elliptic curve with a divisor-sum condition. Krichever\textquotesingle s 1983 survey, \S1.3, identifies a closely matching algebra of matrix Baker--Akhiezer functions; the filtration remains a reconstruction. The 1982 joint Peierls paper confirms the collaboration, but supplies only thematic context for the surviving fragment.
